sections.h2: Who to call about a Seminole County property tax question
sections.html:
Three elected offices split the work. One values the property, one collects the money and one records the deed. Calling the right one first saves a few days.

  • Property Appraiser: 1101 E. 1st Street, Sanford, open weekdays 8 to 5. Call 407-665-7506 for general service or 407-665-7512 about exemptions and fraud.
  • Tax Collector: bills, installment plans, deferral requests and certificates, with payments taken in person, by mail or online.
  • Clerk of Court: deed recording and stamp tax, plus a free property fraud alert that the appraiser encourages every owner to join.

The appraiser's site offers its data free in a downloads area, updated daily in Excel, Access and several GIS formats. Special data requests need 10 business days and may cost labor time.

The county has about 491,884 residents, and two in three households own their home. That leaves roughly a third renting, and a landlord who buys a house never qualifies for homestead, so a seller marketing a rental should be ready to hand over the parcel's tax history.

The $32 billion spread between market and taxable value is what exemptions and caps hold back. A long-held homestead sits well under market on the roll, so a buyer starts from a different place than you do.

Filing is split into two windows: January 1 to March 1 for the current year, then pre-filing from March 2 to December 31 for the next year. The appraiser urges early filing to avoid lines.

A fall buyer can pre-file right away, while a February buyer has very little room before the March 1 cutoff. Requests to split or combine parcels, or to record plats, wait until the current year's taxes are paid. Email the appraiser once a bill is settled so the request moves.

Voters approved the constitutional amendment on property taxes, and the appraiser links to an explainer. Treat the current bill as unchanged, since the roll already certified for 2026 stands, and use the explainer to plan for later years.

As a seller, just confirm which exemptions the house carries today. A larger exemption reaches a buyer only after that buyer files.

Ownership and use on January 1 fix the assessment. March 1 closes homestead and agricultural filings, April 1 closes business personal property returns, and mid-August brings the TRIM notice with a short petition window.

  • November: bills mailed, board hearings start, and the early-payment discount is at its largest.
  • February: the last month with a discount.
  • April 1: delinquency begins.

When a closing lands in a high-discount month, buyer and seller can agree in writing who keeps the savings.

sections.h2: What happens to Save Our Homes when the house sells
sections.html:
The sale ends your benefits. The buyer is assessed at market value from the next January 1, and none of your cap passes along. If you buy again in Florida, you can carry savings to the new homestead, up to $500,000, provided that home is set up within three years. The 2026 cap is 2.7 percent.

Homestead lapses when a house is rented or abandoned, so call the appraiser before turning a Seminole County house into a rental.

sections.h2: How to appeal a value or a denied exemption
sections.html:
Start by asking the appraiser to review the property record. If the dispute remains, the petition deadline is printed on the August notice. A denied exemption or portability claim has its own shorter window running from the denial letter. Miss it and you wait a full cycle, which hurts when a sale is pending.

  • Read the notice for the exact deadline.
  • Collect recent sales and photos of defects.
  • Ask the title agent how a pending petition affects the closing.

The petition goes through the clerk to the Value Adjustment Board.

Pull the latest bill and TRIM notice so buyers see the exemptions and caps on the parcel. Confirm whether the house had homestead on January 1 and whether any deferral or installment plan is active. Gather the deed, any lender payoff letter and open permits, and copy the TRIM notice that shows the savings you plan to port.

The appraiser also publishes a first-time Florida homebuyer guide and a Property Owner Bill of Rights. A buyer from out of state can read them to learn how homestead filing works before the first January 1 passes. Early gathering shortens the gap between contract and closing.

The state stamp rate applies. Everyone on the deed is answerable for it, so the contract should name who pays. Recording opens at a few dollars a page plus technology add-ons, and a personal representative's deed from a probated estate is not taxable.

sections.h2: Selling with an unpaid tax bill
sections.html:
The title company can pay an open bill from your proceeds. If the bill was sold as a certificate, an investor must also be paid, and that investor must wait two years before pressing you. A homestead owing under $250 has its certificate taken by the county. Ask for a payoff before you list.

  • Payoff statement from the collector.
  • Certificate search by the title agent.
  • Confirmation of any lender escrow.

A cash buyer can skip lender underwriting and close quickly, but it does not skip these payoffs. They come out of your proceeds either way.

Homestead removes up to $50,000 of taxable value in two layers, the second skipping school taxes. Seniors may qualify for more where a local ordinance applies, so ask the appraiser what Seminole has adopted. Owners with a service-connected disability may get further breaks, and deferral requests go to the tax collector by March 31.

Ask about these before you list, because an exemption you qualify for lowers this year's bill and that affects the proration at closing. Bring proof of age, residency or disability to the appraiser's office, and file by March 1 so the benefit applies to the current year. If you sell after January 1 but before filing, the exemption for that year can still be lost, so file first when you can.

Once a buyer is under contract, the title company will ask the collector for a current payoff, and the appraiser can confirm in writing which exemptions are on file. Having both documents in hand makes closing day routine and keeps the buyer from being surprised by a higher bill the following November.

faqs.q: Does a Seminole County sale trigger a reassessment?
faqs.a: Yes. On the next January 1 the house is assessed at market value, and your caps and exemptions stay behind.

faqs.q: When are Seminole County tax bills mailed?
faqs.a: In November, from the tax collector. Proposed-tax notices come first, in mid-August.

faqs.q: Where is Seminole County homestead filed?
faqs.a: At the property appraiser's office, by March 1, on Form DR-501. The home must already be your permanent residence on January 1, and pre-filing opens March 2 for the next year.

faqs.q: How long is the Seminole County appeal window?
faqs.a: You get 25 days from the August notice. The petition, on a DR-486 form, goes through the clerk to the Value Adjustment Board.

faqs.q: Who pays stamp tax on a Seminole County sale?
faqs.a: Every party to the deed is liable under the law, so the sale contract should name who pays. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, handled by the clerk at recording.
